title: Scalable Simulation of Strongly Correlated Electron-Phonon Systems via Non-Gaussian Matrix Product States
abstract: We investigate strongly correlated electron-phonon (e-ph) systems via a non-Gaussian matrix product state method. By combining non-Gaussian states with matrix product states, our method efficiently characterizes the intractable entanglement between strongly correlated electrons and phononic modes of unbounded Hilbert space, enabling scalable simulations across broad parameter regimes. In one-dimensional generalized Hubbard--Holstein (HH) models, we identify a pronounced tendency toward phase separation (PS), an instability relevant to recent angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy observations on doped cuprate chain. In two-dimensional HH models, we construct the phase diagram at half-filling featuring a metallic phase emerging from the competition between non-local phonon-mediated attraction and local Hubbard repulsion. Upon doping, we elucidate the role of soft phonons in stabilizing stripe phases. In the antiferromagnet, the stabilization of the fully filled stripe is attributed to a local retardation effect, wherein the charge order is pinned by phonons, leading to a diminished response to spin fluctuations. In the doped charge-density-wave regime, a novel bipolaronic stripe phase with an enlarged unit cell is stabilized via a non-local retardation effect, where long-range phonon-mediated interactions suppress PS. Our work establishes a systematic route to decoding the e-ph interplay that is crucial for superconductivity.
summary: This work develops a scalable Non-Gaussian Matrix Product State (NGS-MPS) method to simulate strongly correlated electron-phonon systems. By applying this technique to Hubbard-Holstein models, the authors map out complex phase diagrams, revealing how phonon interactions stabilize novel electronic phases like bipolaronic stripes crucial for understanding high-temperature superconductivity.
main_problem: The paper investigates strongly correlated electron-phonon (e-ph) systems to decode the complex interplay between electronic correlations and lattice vibrations, which is crucial for understanding superconductivity.
main_result: In 2D models, they map a phase diagram showing a metallic phase emerging from competition effects, and in doped regimes, stabilize novel bipolaronic stripe phases via non-local retardation effects.
method: They employ a Non-Gaussian Matrix Product State (NGS-MPS) method, which combines NGS with MPS to efficiently characterize the entanglement inherent in these complex e-ph systems.
model_or_system: The study focuses on generalized Hubbard–Holstein (HH) models in 1D and 2D. The Hamiltonian includes electronic hopping ($H_e$), phonon propagation ($H_{ph}$), electron-phonon coupling ($H_{e-ph}$), and electron-electron repulsion ($H_{e-e}$).
key_observables: Phase diagram mapping, identification of metallic, antiferromagnetic (AFM), charge-density-wave (CDW), and bipolaronic stripe phases.
important_parameters: Doping concentration, phonon frequency ($\omega$), electron hopping ($t$), Hubbard repulsion ($U$), and coupling strength ($g$).
main_assumptions: The method is designed to overcome limitations of QMC sign problems and standard TNS methods by using a variational ansatz that preserves key symmetries.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the Hamiltonian components, presents the NGS-MPS methodology (including the variational ansatz and optimization workflow), and then systematically applies this method to analyze 1D and 2D HH models across different doping and filling regimes.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the use of advanced tensor network methods like MPS/NGS for simulating coupled bosonic and fermionic degrees of freedom is highly relevant to open quantum systems modeling in AMO physics.
